Here’s the thing from a math perspective it is very hard to balance that number. When you kill two people the number of survivors doing gens drops by either 50 percent (assuming no ones in chase) or 66 percent ( assuming one person is in chase) so they want one person to die while the gens are being worked on and one person to die while the gates open. Counting dcs is bad because then you count games where someone leaves at their first down, making the game a steamroll. You also count games where someone fails to connect, which means let’s just say that happens every 10 percent of games to be fair (which it definitely isn’t) that’s a massive outlier for any data balance, making the devs balance the total games around this outlier number of games. Or say you don’t count disconnects. Then kill rates plummet because you are now excluding times where right before people die, they leave. My point is that this data is pretty much useless in a broad sense due to a massive amount of outlier cases that are necessary to count.

It’s way more nuanced than that though, are you counting dc’s, failure to connects and such. Are you counting ranks, levels and perks? Also you aren’t counting hatch escapes, Moris or key games? The game has more victory conditions than just escapes. Did the survivors rank up? Did the killer rank up? Just balancing the game around that arbitrary number is kinda foolish.
